clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance on 1933-09-07, the date the order was signed: a one-time determination denying the named applicants' application for exemption from the minimum-wage provision of the Coat and Suit Code. Actor: EO 6274 itself ('be and it is hereby denied'). The order states no later effective date. The repeal of June 14, 1935 is a later event, not the end: the denial commanded nothing that the repeal could end. The applicants' continuing obligation is the code's own operation under its approving order.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6274 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6274-the-matter-the-application-connecticut-garment-manufacturers.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (f8da433a0704...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2024-46, captured 2024-11-10T04:32:34Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6274—In the Matter of the Application of Connecticut Garment Manufacturers Association, for Certain Exemptions from the Coat and Suit Code' and whose date is 1933-09-07; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('September 7, 1933.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6274—In the Matter of the Application of Connecticut Garment Manufacturers Association, for Certain Exemptions from the Coat and Suit Code', 1933-09-07) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 538: 'Application of the Connecticut Garment Manufacturers Association for certain exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Coat and Suit Industry denied. I NRA Codes 731.'). The census register title and the WPA entry both name the Coat and Suit Code and the Connecticut Garment Manufacturers Association (I NRA Codes 731). EO 6274 (September 7, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) records that hearings were granted to the named applicants, who 'have applied for an exemption' from the Code of Fair Competition for the Coat and Suit Industry 'with reference to the minimum wage provided in the said code', adopts the Administrator's report of September 5, 1933 that 'no case of injustice and extreme hardship requiring special treatment has been made out', and orders 'that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be and it is hereby denied'. Legal reading, applying the shared analysis on denials of exemption: the order is a one-time determination. It grants nothing and commands nothing after it issues; its command is exhausted by performance on its date, 1933-09-07. The applicants' continuing obligation after the denial is the Coat and Suit Code's own operation, which the approving order (EO 6242-A of August 4, 1933) governs and which the repeal of June 14, 1935 ended; it is not a surviving command of the denial. The repeal is recorded as a later event, not as the end of the denial.

savings.reason: The denial left nothing to continue: it exhausted itself on September 7, 1933. Liabilities the applicants incurred under the Coat and Suit Code while the code approval was in force are accrued effects of the code, not of this order; the section 5 antitrust exemption for completed action under the code is likewise an accrued effect of the code approval (proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113: the held text does not settle its effect on earlier action). Nothing continues a denial after June 14, 1935.
